scenarios.title: Turn around the traffic
scenarios.objective: Turn into space that avoids a teammate and the defender while keeping the puck protected.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. YOU carries through the middle; F2 is directly ahead and D1 is offset to the inside. The useful turning space is beside the traffic, but it depends on F2's movement.
cues: D1 is offset inside that route.
A side space is visible beside the traffic.

questions.prompt: Who is in YOU's straight-ahead route?

options.text: F2
D1
No one

questions.explanation: F2 is directly ahead of YOU in the scene.

questions.prompt: Which two relationships belong in the turn?

options.text: F2's path ahead
D1's inside position
The promise that the outside space stays open

questions.explanation: The teammate and defender both affect the turn. Re-check the outside space as either moves.

questions.prompt: Arrange this controlled-turn plan.

options.text: See F2 and D1
Move toward the available side space
Protect the puck and re-check the lane

questions.explanation: The turn changes the angle, then the puck and lane must be checked again.

questions.prompt: Move YOU beside the traffic into a possible turning space.
questions.explanation: This point leaves F2 ahead and D1 inside, giving YOU a changed angle without assuming the space is empty later.

questions.prompt: F2 moves toward the same outside space. What should you reconsider?

options.text: A different turn or support lane that avoids crowding F2
Keep turning into F2 because the space was named
Pass blindly through D1

questions.explanation: F2 changing route removes the first turning space. Re-scan for another angle or wait for a usable lane.

questions.prompt: Why must a turn account for F2 as well as D1?
questions.explanation: F2 can occupy or open the turning lane. A good turn keeps both players in the scan so the puck stays protected while the next option changes.

scenarios.title: Receive outside the defender
scenarios.objective: Choose a receiving angle that leaves room to protect the first touch.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. F1 carries on the left side and YOU is ahead, with D1 inside the intended route. F2 is high right. The receiver should present a target F1 can actually reach.
cues: F1 owns the puck on the left.
F2 is a high right option after a controlled reception.

questions.prompt: Which player is closest to YOU's inside shoulder?

options.text: F1
D1
F2

questions.explanation: D1 is inside and near YOU; F1 is the passer.

questions.prompt: Which two checks support receiving wider?

options.text: F1's ability to reach the wider target
D1's distance from the first touch
F2 being present even if no lane exists

questions.explanation: The pass route and defender distance explain the wider target; F2 is only a later read.

questions.prompt: Arrange this reception.

options.text: Scan D1 and F1
Present a reachable wide target
Receive and choose the protected next touch

questions.explanation: The target must be reachable first, then the touch can respond to pressure.

questions.prompt: Move YOU wider and slightly up ice to separate from D1.
questions.explanation: This point opens F1's diagonal lane and changes D1's closing angle.

questions.prompt: The pass arrives behind YOU. What should the plan account for?

options.text: Recover the puck while keeping D1 and F1 in the next scan
Turn forward before locating the puck
Assume F2 can collect it

questions.explanation: The actual puck location changes the first task. Recover under control, then re-read pressure and support.

questions.prompt: What makes a slightly wider target useful in this picture?
questions.explanation: It can separate the first touch from D1 and preserve a protected direction, provided F1 can reach it and the lane stays open.

scenarios.title: Bank the puck off the wall
scenarios.objective: Use a wall option to change the route around a defender, then read the rebound.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. F1 has the puck at the left half wall; D1 sits between F1 and YOU. YOU is nearer the boards and F2 is inside. The wall is a practice surface, not a certain receiver.
cues: D1 blocks the direct half-wall lane.
YOU is near the wall beyond D1.
F2 is inside and D2 is above the play.

questions.prompt: What makes the direct F1-to-YOU lane difficult?

options.text: D1 sits in the line
F2 owns the puck
The wall is behind F1

questions.explanation: D1 is between F1 and YOU in the direct line.

questions.prompt: Which two details matter before using the wall?

options.text: Where the rebound would leave YOU and D1
Whether F2 remains an inside option
That the wall sends the puck to the same spot every time

questions.explanation: The wall changes the route but not the need to read the rebound, pressure, and inside support.

questions.prompt: Arrange a wall-option plan.

options.text: See D1 and the wall space
Choose a reachable bank point
Read the rebound before the next touch

questions.explanation: The route around D1 is only useful if the rebound and next lane remain controllable.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a receiving point along the wall beyond D1.
questions.explanation: This point creates a new wall relationship while keeping F2 and D2 in the wider scene.

questions.prompt: D1 turns toward the boards before F1 releases. What should you revisit?

options.text: Whether the wall route or F2 lane is now more reachable
Bank the puck without looking because D1 moved
Pass through D1 to the original spot

questions.explanation: D1's turn changes both routes. Compare the wall rebound with F2's inside availability before choosing.

questions.prompt: How is a wall option different from simply passing through D1?
questions.explanation: It changes the puck route around the defender and creates a new rebound to read. The option remains conditional on the rebound and support.

scenarios.title: Recover the pass that drifts
scenarios.objective: Find the actual puck location after a pass misses its intended target.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. F1 has sent a pass toward YOU, but the puck is loose below the intended line. D1 is ahead of the loose puck and F2 is to the inside.
cues: The puck is loose below YOU.
D1 is ahead of the puck.
F1 and F2 remain visible support options.

questions.prompt: Where is the puck compared with YOU?

options.text: Below YOU
With D1
Above F2

questions.explanation: The loose puck is below YOU and has no owner.

questions.prompt: Which two questions help a useful recovery?

options.text: Can YOU reach the actual puck before D1?
Which teammate can support after control?
Did the intended pass arrive at the planned spot?

questions.explanation: The actual puck and pressure determine recovery; the intended spot is no longer the live cue.

questions.prompt: Arrange this missed-pass response.

options.text: Locate the actual puck and D1
Approach with control
Re-scan F1 and F2 after recovery

questions.explanation: The recovery begins from the real puck location and updates once possession is possible.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the loose puck while keeping D1 in sight.
questions.explanation: This point approaches the actual loose puck and preserves a view up ice.

questions.prompt: D1 reaches the loose puck first. What changed?

options.text: D1 may now be the carrier, so support and pressure jobs switch
YOU still owns the pass
The puck returned to F1

questions.explanation: D1 reaching first changes possession. Re-read F1, F2, and the net-side risk before choosing your job.

questions.prompt: What could you say to F1 after the pass misses?
questions.explanation: Name the actual puck location and D1's pressure, then call your next support or recovery cue so F1 can adjust the next route.

scenarios.title: Open the shooting lane
scenarios.objective: Reassess a shooting lane when a defender moves toward another attacker.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. YOU controls the puck high in the right-side lane; D1 is between YOU and the net. F2 is low and wide. If D1 moves, the lane and support read change together.
cues: D1 occupies the straight shooting line.
The net and goalie are visible, but a shot outcome is not proven.

options.text: F2
D1
The goalie only

questions.prompt: Which two cues should be read together?

options.text: D1's position in the lane
F2's availability if D1 moves
A promise that the lane will clear

questions.explanation: The defender and teammate create the choice. A lane only becomes useful if it remains open after the movement.

questions.prompt: Arrange this high-lane decision.

options.text: Identify D1 and F2
Check whether a lane or pass opens
Choose a shot, pass or protected touch

questions.explanation: The carrier waits for the updated lane, then chooses among the still-reachable options.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a shooting angle outside D1 while keeping F2 visible.
questions.explanation: This point changes the line from YOU to the net and keeps F2 in the scene; it does not certify a shot.

questions.prompt: D1 moves toward F2 and the direct lane opens. What deserves a new look?

options.text: Whether the open lane supports a shot or a pass now
Force a shot without checking the goalie or lane
Ignore F2 because D1 moved

questions.explanation: D1's movement changes the lane, but the carrier still reads space and support before choosing.

questions.prompt: Why can the slot and half wall lead to different choices here?
questions.explanation: The slot has a different relationship to D1, the net, and F2. Explain which lane is visible now and what movement would make another option safer.
